The percentage of persons retained in care for 0, 1, 2, and 3 years during 2011–2013 was determined.
Overall, 43% of all persons included in the analysis were retained in HIV care for all 3 years during 2011–2013.
A lower proportion of blacks were retained during 2011–2013 (38%), compared with Hispanics (50%) and whites (49%).
Differences in consistent retention in care by race/ethnicity persisted when stratified by sex or transmission category
Results were statistically adjusted for missing information on transmission category using multiple imputation
This analysis includes persons aged ≥13 years who received a diagnosis of HIV infection in 2010
CDC analyzed data from NHSS reported through July 2015 from 12 jurisdictions

methods_quotes.q: The percentage of persons retained in care for 0, 1, 2, and 3 years during 2011–2013 was determined.
Differences in consistent retention in care were assessed by race/ethnicity, sex, transmission category, and state of residence at diagnosis.
Results were statistically adjusted for missing information on transmission category using multiple imputation
Persons retained in care for all 3 years were considered to be consistently retained in HIV care.
